title: Higher stack direct images as sheafified fibre cohomology presheaves
statement:
Work in the universes and small-skeleton convention of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $h:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ a morphism of algebraic stacks over $S$ [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]. Use their inherited big fppf sites, categories fibred in groupoids, $2$-fibre products and structure sheaves of [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra, def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Also use the big etale sites on the same objects and arrows, with coverings lying over jointly surjective etale scheme maps [def-weil-etale-morphism] and the same structure sheaves. Fix $\tau\in\{\mathrm{et},\mathrm{fppf}\}$ and a structure-module sheaf $M$ on $\mathcal X_\tau$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For a test object $y$ of $\mathcal Y$ over $V$, put $\mathcal X_y=\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}(\mathit{Sch}/V)$ and let $p_y:\mathcal X_y\to\mathcal X$ be the projection; $p_y^{-1}M$ means precomposition, with the unchanged structure ring on each scheme test object. Direct image has the section formula $(h_{\tau,*}M)(y)=\Gamma(\mathcal X_y,p_y^{-1}M)$. For each $q\geq0$, define
$$P^q_{\tau,M}(y)=H^q(\mathcal X_{y,\tau},p_y^{-1}M),$$
where cohomology and higher direct images are computed using injective resolutions in all structure-module sheaves [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. The restriction maps of $P^q_{\tau,M}$ are the canonical cohomology restriction maps from base change of test objects, and the action of $\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$ is induced by pullback of functions. Then the canonical cocycle-to-cohomology-sheaf map induces an isomorphism of module sheaves
$$(P^q_{\tau,M})^{\#_\tau}\xrightarrow{\sim}R^q h_{\tau,*}M,$$
where module sheafification is [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. This is natural in $M$ and compatible with the indicated restrictions and scalar actions. There is no representability, quasi-compactness, quasi-separatedness, quasi-coherence or flatness assumption on $h$ or $M$.

source.place: Tag 075G (lemma-pushforward-restriction), its formula and injective-resolution proof; naturality is induced by restrictions and resolution maps in that proof.

proof.text: Use the resolution-existence clause of lem-sfb-module-resolution-derived-presheaf-comparison on the chosen small ringed site $\mathcal X_\tau$ to choose $M[0]\to I^\bullet$ with injective module terms and $I^n=0$ for $n<0$. Put $K^\bullet=h_{\tau,*}I^\bullet$. By lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-map-via-lift, $R^qh_{\tau,*}M\cong\mathcal H^q(K^\bullet)$. Here $h_*$ is additive and left exact: by its section formula a section of a kernel is a compatible family of sections in the kernels, and kernels of modules are sectionwise by def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category. Let $L^\bullet$ be the underlying presheaf complex of $K^\bullet$, and put $Q^q=\ker d_L^q/\operatorname{im}d_L^{q-1}$ in module presheaves. These kernels and quotients are sectionwise: the usual module kernels and quotients inherit the semilinear restriction maps and satisfy the universal properties object by object. Thus $Q^q(y)=H^q(K^\bullet(y))$, with the induced restrictions and $\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$-action. For $q=0$ the incoming term is zero.

For each test object $y/V$, lem-sfb-stack-test-fibre-restriction-injectives makes $p_y^{-1}I^\bullet$ an injective resolution of $p_y^{-1}M$: exactness preserves the augmented resolution and each term remains injective. Consequently the injective-resolution computation in lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-map-via-lift gives
$$P^q_{\tau,M}(y)\cong H^q\Gamma(\mathcal X_y,p_y^{-1}I^\bullet)=H^q(K^\bullet(y))=Q^q(y).$$
The middle equality is the direct-image section formula in the statement, degree by degree. For an arrow $a:y'\to y$, let $r_a:\mathcal X_{y'}\to\mathcal X_y$ be base change. On each term the restriction of a compatible family $(s_z)_z$ is $(s_{r_a(z')})_{z'}$. Since $p_y r_a=p_{y'}$ up to the specified fibre-product identification, this is exactly the restriction map of $h_*I^n$. Applying cohomology therefore gives the canonical cohomology restriction, computed on these restricted resolutions, so the displayed identifications form a presheaf isomorphism $P^q_{\tau,M}\cong Q^q$. A function $b\in\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$ acts on a section over $T\to V$ by multiplication by its pullback to $T$. The differentials are module-linear, so cycles and boundaries inherit this action. For $a$ over $u:V'\to V$, the equality $(bs)|_{y'}=u^*(b)s|_{y'}$ holds already on the section complexes. Hence the presheaf isomorphism is an isomorphism of structure-module presheaves.

Module sheafification on $\mathcal Y_\tau$ is exact by lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-module-sheafification-exact. Apply lem-sp-exact-functor-preserves-homology (c) to the three terms around degree $q$ of $L^\bullet$. It gives
$$(Q^q)^{\#_\tau}\cong\mathcal H^q((L^\bullet)^{\#_\tau}).$$
Each $L^n$ underlies the sheaf $K^n$. The universal property in def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification identifies $(L^n)^{\#_\tau}$ with $K^n$: extend the identity map to the sheafification, and both composites are identities by uniqueness. Uniqueness also makes these identifications commute with differentials. Combining with steps 1 and 2 gives
$$(P^q_{\tau,M})^{\#_\tau}\cong(Q^q)^{\#_\tau}\cong\mathcal H^q(K^\bullet)\cong R^qh_{\tau,*}M.$$
The homology comparison in (c) respects cycle inclusions and quotient projections. Its map before sheafification sends a cycle to its class in the cohomology sheaf. Thus this is precisely the asserted canonical cocycle map. Every arrow is a module morphism, so the isomorphism respects the indicated scalar actions.

For a module morphism $v:M\to N$, choose a second such resolution $N\to J^\bullet$. The statement of lem-weil-pbc-injective-resolution-lift-exists supplies an augmentation-preserving module chain map $t:I^\bullet\to J^\bullet$ lifting $v$. Its restrictions $p_y^{-1}t$ are maps of the injective resolutions from step 2. By lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-map-via-lift, the maps on fibre cohomology and on $R^qh_*$ are computed respectively by $H^q\Gamma(p_y^{-1}t)$ and $\mathcal H^q(h_*t)$. Both send a represented cycle $z$ to the class represented by $t^q(z)$; this commutes with the restriction formula in step 2. Naturality of the exact-functor homology comparison in lem-sp-exact-functor-preserves-homology (c), followed by the uniqueness of sheafification in def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification, therefore yields $R^qh_*(v)\circ\sigma_M=\sigma_N\circ(P^q(v))^{\#_\tau}$. Taking $v=\mathrm{id}_M$ with two different resolutions identifies the construction for both choices with the identity maps of the fixed derived groups and higher-image sheaf, by the same derived-map formula. Thus the isomorphism is independent of the resolution and natural in $M$. All constructions have been in all structure-module sheaves; no geometric finiteness, representability, quasi-coherence or flatness condition was used.

This is stable pointed-curve extension, not stable modification of a specified target pair. Affine-chart proof of the projective PGL quotient: Affine PGL quotients with closed orbits and zero-dimensional stabilizers. Supporting affine-quotient step: Finite inertia gives an adequate coarse moduli space. Supporting input to the finite-inertia coarse-space construction: Passage from invariant global power liftings on the affine rank charts to adequate moduli spaces, then etale descent to the glued map. Flat scalar-section comparison needed in the descent of a power lying in the image of a global algebra map; this does not assert adequate-moduli locality. General cohomological input: preservation of locally quasi-coherent modules and flat comparison maps under qcqs stack direct images. Supporting input: Etale-fppf comparison under locally finitely presented flat comparisons. Sheafified fibre-cohomology formula used to assemble the higher-direct-image comparison.
